items.description: IT之家 11 月 16 日消息，苹果中国官网现已更新 iPhone Duo 手机送货上门时间，从 2027 年 1 月 23 日提前至 2026 年 12 月 15 日至 2026 年 12 月 22 日。 IT之家注意到，目前国内多家 Apple Store 零售店已支持 iPhone Duo 部分版本直接购买和到店取货，如果用户想尽快购买手机，可以尝试在官网预约后自行到店取货，无需等待官方送货。 参考IT之家先前报道，有消息称 苹果 iPhone Duo 折叠屏手机首销期（首销日 + 后三天）的 SO（销量）接近 200K（20 万）。 iPhone Duo 采用可折叠设计，配备了苹果迄今面积最大的 iPhone 显示屏。展开状态下，它是迄今最薄的 iPhone，内置显示屏面积比 iPhone 18 Pro Max 还要大 50%；闭合状态下，5.4 英寸外屏以小巧紧凑的机身设计，提供了相当于 iPhone 18 Pro 90% 的屏幕显示面积。

items.title: 英国出台网络安全新规：平台必须主动识别并删除儿童色情内容
items.description: IT之家 11 月 16 日消息，据路透社报道，英国通信管理局（Ofcom）周一宣布收紧网络儿童安全监管规定，要求各类网络平台加大打击儿童性虐待内容和诱骗行为的力度。此举也为英国计划实施的 16 岁以下青少年社交媒体禁令铺路。 根据新规定，社交媒体平台、文件共享服务、色情网站及其他在线服务预计将从 2027 年初开始承担新的监管义务，具体实施时间仍需获得英国议会批准。 新规要求， 相关平台必须封禁制作、上传或传播儿童性虐待内容的用户 。同时， 平台还需要扩大相关技术的应用范围，主动检测并删除已知的非法图片 ；在某些情况下，还必须部署自动化工具，识别此前尚未发现的相关内容。 IT之家注意到，英国今年 6 月宣布，计划禁止 16 岁以下青少年使用 TikTok、Instagram、Snapchat 和 X 等社交媒体平台。英国政府当时表示，这些措施将有助于“把童年还给孩子们”。 Ofcom 表示，周一公布的新措施是应对网络儿童性虐待内容问题所必需的。该机构指出，相关非法内容在网络上的传播规模庞大，而人工智能技术的发展进一步加剧了这一问题。 Ofcom 网络安全部门负责人奥利弗 · 格里菲思

The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 others. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.” “Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.” Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return .) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem. Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here . Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn’t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days.

items.title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
items.description: The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. The petition states that its signers are “concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process” and demands that the board “bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.” It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public. “Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the petition says. Huang resigned on Thursday , four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs . Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company’s interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia’s stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang’s departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding .

items.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.description: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Last month, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Soon after, privacy-focused AI assistant Ollie announced its shutdown, too, citing competition in the market. “We got close, but ultimately couldn’t keep up,” co-founder and CEO Bill Lennon said on X . Aside from Character.ai and Ollie, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. items.author: Kate Park
items.content: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. items.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.description: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
items.author: Marina Temkin, Dominic-Madori Davis
items.content: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor , pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.description: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday. That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago , led by IVP. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence. With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. It also promises that LangSmith will contain agent behavior and is easy to use. True, there are plenty of other startups pitching similar advantages these days and also doing well ( case in point is newcomer Mintive ). However, LangChain has had a head start and now claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including big-name startups like Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, and enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce. items.title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
items.description: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: ChatGPT can now shop for you. On Friday, OpenAI launched a new wallet feature that lets its agents, called dots , help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf. The option will initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express. OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction. The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app. Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf. It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own.
